title: Polish public support for defense financing is positive but divided across SAFE and NBP funding routes

denominator.unit: adult residents of Poland; CATI 80% and CAWI 20%

observations.method: Translation-neutral extraction of the published CBOS Flash 11/2026. The fieldwork dates, mixed CATI/CAWI design, sample denominator, overall shares, ideology subgroup shares, and cross-tab route preferences are retained as separate survey measures.
observations.uncertainty: This is cross-sectional self-reported public opinion. Subgroup base sizes and sampling errors are not reproduced here; ideology and potential-electorate groupings are survey classifications. The result does not identify weapon-specific preferences or subsequent behavior.
observations.subgroup: Adult residents of Poland; political-ideology and potential-electorate groupings as reported by CBOS.
observations.counterinterpretation: Support for a financing route does not equal support for Barracuda-500M, a local-production agreement, a particular supplier, or a procurement order. The political split may reflect broader EU, sovereignty, fiscal, and party-identification views.

related_sources.claim: Barracuda realization watchpoint supplies the separate implementation, production, and delivery boundary.
Normalized local evidence note preserves the CBOS survey denominator, percentages, and interpretation boundary.
CBOS primary survey supplies dated Polish public judgment about alternative defense-financing routes and their political division.

boundary: This record measures Polish public judgment about defense-financing routes. It does not measure Barracuda-500M demand, public reception of the local-production agreement, production, delivery, trust change, political action, or geopolitical leverage. The observed support shares are judgments, not behavioral outcomes.
